subject: Proposed MAP & acceptance test plan for CuraHealth evaluation
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@curahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP & acceptance test plan for CuraHealth evaluation

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great conversation. As discussed, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short acceptance-test checklist we think will make the evaluation objective and fast to run. High-level ask: can your team review the MAP and the evaluation acceptance tests and confirm (a) whether these criteria map to your success metrics, and (b) whether procurement timelines below are realistic?

Quick summary of the proposed plan:
- 4-week evaluation window (pilot traffic + 2 integration sprints)
- Acceptance tests focused on 3 KPIs: 95th percentile latency under 250ms, intent concordance >= 92% across sampled prompts, and embedding recall >= 0.88 for the provided test set
- Exit gates: pass all smoke tests (automated), no more than 2 high-severity defects, and procurement/contract signed for pilot capacity by week 3

Attachments: CuraHealth-MAP-v2.xlsx (MAP with owners & dates), eval-acceptance-tests.md (test checklist), SLA-draft.pdf (baseline SLA).

Proposed next steps:
1) Jordan — can you confirm alignment on success metrics by Mon 15 Jun?
2) Laura — can you own the technical onboarding tasks and the smoke-test runbook?
3) Marissa — I’ll coordinate legal/procurement and push the SLA draft to DocuSign.

If that works, we’ll lock dates and schedule the first integration sync for Tue 16 Jun.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0193

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@curahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, CuraHealth Procurement <procurement@curahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance test plan for CuraHealth evaluation

Rafael — thanks for the materials and the clear plan. We reviewed with product and procurement this morning; overall looks good and matches what we need. A couple of clarifications from our side before we sign off: 

1) Intent concordance definition — can you confirm you’ll run the concordance check against the clinical-intent prompt set we shared (sheet: CH-intents.csv)? We need the sampling method documented.
2) Embedding recall threshold — 0.88 is acceptable if the dataset used is the one in the shared drive. We’ll validate on our side but would like an instrumentation hook to reproduce results later.
3) Procurement ask — procurement needs the SLA-draft.pdf to show availability and data residency clauses. Can Marissa loop in her legal contact?

Assuming those clarifications are addressed, we can agree to the MAP and start the integration work on Tue 16 Jun. Procurement target: have a pilot order form signed by Fri 26 Jun.

Jordan
Head of Product Integrations
CuraHealth
jordan.ellis@curahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: CuraHealth Procurement <procurement@curahealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@curahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance test plan for CuraHealth evaluation

Hi procurement team / Jordan — looping in our contracts lead (legal@redwood.ai) separately but wanted to confirm a few operational points from the SLA side so procurement can move the order form: 

- Data residency: Redwood will provision the CuraHealth pilot in our us-east region and will ensure no customer data is replicated to other regions during the pilot.
- Availability commitment for pilot (best-effort): 99.5% for pilot tier; production SLA options are documented in SLA-draft.pdf.
- Audit logs & evidence: we can export per-request audit logs for the evaluation window; sample export will be shared to the Drive folder once onboarding completes.

Rafael — I added comments to CuraHealth-MAP-v2.xlsx (owners column) and to eval-acceptance-tests.md. Procurement: if these items look fine we can proceed to signature — Rafael will confirm pricing and the order form.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Contracts & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@curahealth.com>, CuraHealth Procurement <procurement@curahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 20:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance test plan for CuraHealth evaluation — confirmed timeline and kickoff

Jordan / procurement — thanks for the quick review and the questions. Summary of updates and final asks before kickoff: 

- Intent concordance: Redwood will run concordance against CH-intents.csv using stratified sampling (n=500) and publish the sampling script and seed in the Drive folder.
- Embedding recall: we'll provide the evaluation harness and notebook to reproduce the recall calculation; target >= 0.88 on the shared dataset.
- Procurement: Marissa will send the final SLA and order form via DocuSign by Fri 19 Jun; target signature by Fri 26 Jun to keep pilot start on Mon 29 Jun.

Kickoff sync scheduled: Tue 16 Jun — 11:00 AM ET (team integration + smoke-test dry run). Confirmed attendees: Jordan, Rafael, Laura, Marissa, plus CuraHealth engineering (joining link in calendar invite).

If procurement needs any additional items for the order form — please flag by EOD Fri 19 Jun. Looking forward to a fast evaluation.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

> Attachment stubs: CuraHealth-MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-acceptance-tests.md (markdown checklist), SLA-draft.pdf (PDF)
